votes.evidence: Premise confirmed by tracing the callers. PR #75215 body (fetched via gh) says "at least one of the assigned users has `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` enabled" (Changes), "checks whether any assigned reviewer opted in" (Case 1 step 3), and "nobody is opted in, so no review runs" (Case 3 step 2). The code in the worktree gates on exactly one user: /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:206 `acting = next((user for user in resolved if user.id == task_created_by_id), resolved[0])` returns a single id; `handle_task_run_saved` at receivers.py:111-114 loads `ReviewUserSettings.load(instance.team_id, acting_user_id)` for that one user and checks `review_inbox_prs` (114) and `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` (125); `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` at receivers.py:151-156 does the same single-user check for the webhook leg, which products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:205-207 treats as `opted_out=True` when None. No path iterates the resolved reviewer set for toggles. The single-owner model is deliberate and tested: receivers.py:160-173 docstring ("the **first** resolved reviewer is canonical (maintainer decisions, 2026-07-02/03)"), and products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:228-237 `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review` asserts that with reviewers ["bob","alice"], bob (canonical) opted out and alice opted in, no review starts ("a later reviewer's opt-in must not hijack"). That test is the exact scenario the PR body claims would run a review. The mismatch is therefore real, and it is the description that is wrong, not the code.
votes.refutation: Tried to find an any-of check somewhere in the chain (receivers.py, the stamphog resolver call at tasks.py:201-207, the inbox_hooks contract returning a single `int | None`) and found none. Tried to read the PR body as loosely compatible with single-owner semantics, but "at least one of the assigned users" and "any assigned reviewer" are explicit any-of claims, and the shipped test suite asserts the opposite behavior. The refutation fails on the mismatch itself; what it does establish is that the code is coherent, documented, and tested as intended, so the only actionable fix is the PR description wording. Because nothing incorrect ships in code (the cited receivers.py lines behave as their docstrings say), this is a documentation-only inaccuracy in the PR body rather than a should_fix defect; the separate user-facing confusion (a non-canonical assignee toggling on and seeing nothing) is inherent in the chosen design and is covered by other findings about UI copy, not by this one.

votes.evidence: Premise confirmed on both sides. PR #75215 body (fetched via gh): "## Changes — ... at least one of the assigned users has `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` enabled"; Case 1 step 3 "checks whether any assigned reviewer opted in"; Case 2 "someone is still opted in"; Case 3 "everyone turns the toggle off ... nobody is opted in". Code in the worktree gates on exactly one user: /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:151-156 (`resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` loads `ReviewUserSettings` for the single `acting_user_id` and returns None if that one row's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` is off); receivers.py:110-126 does the same for both toggles on the initial trigger; `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` receivers.py:206-207 picks `task_created_by` if in the resolved set else `resolved[0]` and never iterates the others' settings. The webhook re-review leg consumes that single id via products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:201-207 and the hook contract in products/stamphog/backend/facade/inbox_hooks.py:22-24 is defined as returning one user id. Existing tests pin the single-reviewer semantic as intended, i.e. the opposite of "any assigned": products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:229-239 `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review` asserts no review runs when the canonical reviewer is off and a second assigned reviewer (alice) is on; test_inbox_trigger.py:256-268 `test_non_assigned_requester_follows_the_canonical_reviewer` asserts the same for an opted-in non-assigned creator; test_inbox_trigger.py:324-379 checks the stamphog toggle through that same single acting reviewer. Every in-repo contract surface matches the code, not the PR body: products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:84-86 ("whose acting reviewer opted in via ReviewHog's per-user toggle"), products/stamphog/README.md:14 ("gated by the acting reviewer's per-user `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle"), models.py:268-280 docstring, api/settings.py:27-33 help_text, and the UI copy "Let Stamphog review your Inbox PRs" (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1053-1057).
votes.refutation: Attempted refutation: the mismatch could be dismissed if the PR body's "at least one assigned user" were merely loose prose for the same behavior, or if the code actually iterated all assignees. Neither holds. The tests at test_inbox_trigger.py:229-239 explicitly assert that a second assigned reviewer's opt-in does NOT trigger a review when the canonical one is off, so "any assigned reviewer opted in" is provably false as a description of the shipped gate, and the docstring at receivers.py:159-173 records the single-owner model as a deliberate maintainer decision. What the refutation does establish is that the defect is confined to the PR body: the code, its tests, AGENTS.md, README, model docstring, serializer help_text and UI copy are all mutually consistent on "the acting reviewer's toggle". No code change is warranted and nothing incorrect ships in the repository, so this is a real but minor documentation correction (fix the PR description wording), not a should_fix defect.
